text:
anya: Quick ask — can someone run a focused micro-benchmark comparing streaming vs sync when invoking tool calls that return structured JSON? I think serialization + tool plumbing is adding nontrivial overhead on short responses.

devon: Sure — what are the payload sizes and what counts as "structured" here? nested objects, arrays?

matt: I can run this on dedicated-qa (A100). Want me to include both warm and cold KV cache?

anya: Good Qs. Keep it small/typical for our router: ~1-2 short turns, tool returns a compact JSON (3 keys, one array of 3 items). Example body: ```json
{"query":"weather in sf","tools":[{"name":"geo","params":{"lat":37.7,"lon":-122.4}}],"response_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"temp":{"type":"number"},"conds":{"type":"string"},"alerts":{"type":"array"}}}}
```

devon: Perfect. Compare: 
- streaming with toolcall (stream tokens as they arrive)
- sync function call (complete output after generation)
- streaming + structured-serializer (compact mode)

sara: Also include 1) batch size 1 vs 8, 2) short max_tokens (32) to emphasize per-call overhead, and 3) tracing enabled so we can get breakdown. Use the perf tracing flag: `REDWOOD_TRACE=1`

perf-bot: FYI baseline from last run (2026-01-12): streaming+toolcall median p50=42ms, p95=120ms on A100-dedicated-qa. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/20260112/stream-toolcall-baseline

matt: Plan: spin up a 4-run matrix (stream/sync x cache warm/cold) x batch sizes {1,8}. I'll post `rt-bench` commands and raw traces here. Expected run time ~20m.

matt: Command I'm using: ```bash
rt-bench --model redwood-open-7b --mode streaming --toolchain tool-runner-v2 --payload sample_small.json --max-tokens 32 --batch 1 --tracing out.json
```

anya: Please include one run with our compact serializer flag: `--serializer compact` — that was the suspected win.

ryan: If results look promising, I can draft a tiny PR to flip serializer by default for toolcall small-payloads. Will need your traces to justify.

matt: Results posted (quick summary): 
- streaming + default-serializer, batch=1, warm cache: p50=46ms, p95=135ms
- sync functioncall, batch=1, warm cache: p50=39ms, p95=98ms
- streaming + compact-serializer, batch=1, warm cache: p50=33ms, p95=85ms
Notes: compact serializer shaves ~25-30% on short responses. Batch=8 amortizes overhead but streaming still slightly higher tail due to framing. Full traces: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1782345678/bench

anya: Awesome, thanks. Can you attach the per-span breakdown (serialization vs network vs runtime)? I'll add to the rollout notes.

matt: Attached spans in the run link: serialization ~12-16ms, network/frame ~8-12ms, inference compute ~15-18ms for these short tokens.

devon: Great data. Let's prototype defaulting to compact serializer for toolcall outputs under 128 tokens and measure in canary.

anya: Okay — next steps: 1) devon/ryan sketch PR for serializer rule, 2) matt add an A/B canary job in the console for next week, 3) sara add perf regression alert to watch p95 for streaming-toolcall.

ryan: On it, I'll ping for review when draft is up.

matt: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
